items.title:
Anthropic shares fell below their $83 IPO price in premarket trading Tuesday, hitting $82.20, down about 6% from Monday's close of $87.64.
The AI company began trading on Nasdaq last Thursday after pricing its IPO at $83 a share.
items.title_ja:
アンスロピック株は火曜日の市場前取引で公開価格の83ドルを下回り、82.20ドルとなり、月曜日の終値87.64ドルから​​約6％下落した。
このAI企業は、IPOの価格を1株当たり83ドルとした後、先週の木曜日にナスダックで取引を開始した。

items.title:
Avicena, a startup building microLED-based optical links to move data between chips in AI systems, has raised $100 million in a Series C.
Investors include AMD Ventures, Samsung Catalyst Fund, SK hynix Ventures, Tiger Global, Cerberus and Intervest.
items.title_ja:
AI システムのチップ間でデータを移動するための microLED ベースの光リンクを構築する新興企業 Avicena が、シリーズ C で 1 億ドルを調達した。
投資家には、AMD Ventures、Samsung Catalyst Fund、SK hynix Ventures、Tiger Global、Cerberus、Intervest が含まれます。

items.title:
Albert Manifold, ousted as BP chair, will join the board of temporary power provider Aggreko after its IPO, the FT reports.
Aggreko has filed to list on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker AGKO.
items.title_ja:
BP会長を解任されたアルバート・マニフォールド氏は、IPO後に臨時電力会社アグレコの取締役会に加わるとFT紙が報じた。
アグレコはティッカーAGKOでニューヨーク証券取引所への上場を申請した。

items.title:
Compass Group confirms plans to move its primary listing from London to the US, with the switch expected in 2028.
The FTSE 100 caterer will consult shareholders and keep a secondary UK listing. Its board says the US has become its natural long-term listing venue.
items.title_ja:
コンパス・グループは、主要上場先をロンドンから米国に移す計画を確認しており、移行は2028年になる見込みだ。
FTSE 100のケータリング会社は株主と協議し、英国の二次上場を維持する予定だ。取締役会は、米国が自然な長期上場地となったと述べている。

items.title:
Investment firm HLD Europe plans to take control of French care-home operator Clariane with Crédit Agricole Assurances, followed by a tender offer at €4.60 a share, a 38.3% premium.
The two already hold about 53%. The offer is not meant to delist Clariane.
items.title_ja:
投資会社HLDヨーロッパは、クレディ・アグリコル・アシュアランスとともにフランスの介護施設運営会社クラリアンの経営権を取得し、その後1株当たり4.60ユーロ（38.3％のプレミアム）で株式公開買い付けを行う計画だ。
両者はすでに約53％を保有している。この提案は、クラリアンを上場廃止にすることを目的としたものではありません。

items.title:
Singapore's StarHub will buy Keppel's privately held telecom operator M1 in an all-share deal valuing M1 at an enterprise value of S$1.36 billion.
StarHub will issue about 651.7 million new shares to M1's shareholders. The combined group will have an enterprise value of about $3.9 billion, Reuters says.
items.title_ja:
シンガポールのスターハブはケッペルの非公開通信事業者M1を全株取引で買収し、M1の企業価値は13億6000万シンガポールドルとなる。
スターハブはＭ１の株主に約６億５１７０万株の新株を発行する。ロイター通信によると、統合後のグループの企業価値は約39億ドルになるという。

items.title:
AustralianSuper, Reliance Worldwide's largest shareholder with a stake of about 17%, will support Brookfield's takeover of the SharkBite plumbing parts maker, Reuters reports.
Brookfield agreed in September to pay US$3.38 a share in cash, valuing Reliance at about US$2.9 billion including debt.
items.title_ja:
約17％の株式を保有するリライアンス・ワールドワイドの筆頭株主であるオーストラリアンスーパーは、ブルックフィールドによる配管部品メーカーシャークバイトの買収を支持するとロイター通信が報じた。
ブルックフィールドは9月、リライアンスの価値を負債を含めて約29億ドルと評価し、1株当たり3.38ドルを現金で支払うことに同意した。

items.title:
DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng is now worth $55 billion after the Chinese AI lab's latest fundraising, according to Bloomberg.
Separately, Chinese Q&A platform Zhihu said Monday that a fund has invested in DeepSeek.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグによると、ディープシーク創設者の梁文峰氏は、中国AI研究所の最新の資金調達により、現在550億ドルの価値があるという。
これとは別に、中国のQ&AプラットフォームZhihuは月曜日、ファンドがDeepSeekに投資したと発表した。

items.title:
Clariant confirms it is in talks to acquire Ashland in partnership with private equity firm Clayton, Dubilier & Rice, following Bloomberg's report of the discussions.
Clariant says there is no certainty a deal will be agreed.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグの交渉報道を受けて、クラリアントはプライベートエクイティ会社クレイトン・デュビリエ・アンド・ライスと提携してアシュランド買収交渉を行っていることを認めた。
クラリアントは、合意に達する確証はないと述べた。

items.title:
A Macquarie Asset Management-led consortium has agreed to buy EDOTCO's Asia-Pacific telecom tower businesses, including its towers in the Philippines, for $1.2 billion.
EDOTCO is the tower unit of Malaysia's Axiata Group.
items.title_ja:
マッコーリー・アセット・マネジメント主導のコンソーシアムは、フィリピンのタワーを含むEDOTCOのアジア太平洋通信タワー事業を12億ドルで買収することで合意した。
EDOTCO は、マレーシアの Axiata グループのタワー部門です。

items.title:
Ford is making a minority investment in Revolution Space, a private spacecraft maker chaired by former NASA Administrator Daniel Goldin, to help scale production of its spacecraft.
Terms were not disclosed. Ford says the move is part of a push into markets less cyclical than autos.
items.title_ja:
フォードは、宇宙船の生産規模拡大を支援するため、元NASA長官ダニエル・ゴールディン氏が会長を務める民間宇宙船メーカー、レボリューション・スペースに少数出資している。
条件は明らかにされていない。フォードは、この動きは自動車ほど景気循環のない市場への参入の一環であると述べている。

items.title: Eli Lilly agrees to acquire LoQus23 Therapeutics, a private developer of Huntington's disease drugs, for up to $725 million, Reuters and Dow Jones report.
items.title_ja: ロイター通信とダウ・ジョーンズの報道によると、イーライリリーはハンチントン病治療薬の民間開発会社であるLoQus23 Therapeuticsを最大7億2500万ドルで買収することに合意した。

items.title:
Quantum Space, the maneuverable spacecraft maker led by former NASA Administrator Jim Bridenstine, has completed its SPAC merger at a pro forma equity value of about $958 million.
It raised about $300 million in two private placements at closing, and shares are expected to begin trading on the NYSE as QSPC on Tuesday.
items.title_ja:
元NASA長官のジム・ブライデンスタイン氏が率いる操縦可能な宇宙船メーカー、クォンタム・スペースは、約9億5,800万ドルの推定株式価値でSPACの合併を完了した。
同社は取引終了時点で2件の私募で約3億ドルを調達しており、株式は火曜日にQSPCとしてニューヨーク証券取引所で取引が開始される予定だ。

items.title:
Amazon confirms it will acquire AI startup Decart's optimization technology and team, in a deal Bloomberg reports is worth $7.5 billion.
Amazon says the technology will advance chip and model innovation for its customers.
items.title_ja:
ブルームバーグの報道によると、アマゾンはAI新興企業デカートの最適化技術とチームを買収することを確認しており、その買収額は75億ドル相当とブルームバーグは報じている。
アマゾンは、この技術により顧客のチップとモデルの革新が進むと述べている。

ダイヤモンドオンラインにフォスター電機に関するインタビュー記事が掲載されました。
具体的だけれども挑戦的な計画に仕上げていったプロセス、大胆な資本構成の決定に至ったプロセスなど話しています。
投資ファンドとしてどのようなソリューションを投資先に提供できるかという視点で投資活動に取り組んでいる旨お話ししています。
~~~~
フォスター電機のROE（株主資本利益率）は8％弱でした。一方、国債利回りや日本株の投資家が期待するリターンを考えると、社内では資本コストをおおむね11％と試算していました。この水準を上回るリターンを出さなければ、投資家に納得してもらえる経営とはいえません。
26年3月期末に117億円のネットキャッシュを抱え、ROEが8％弱という状態では、どんなに説明を尽くしても、最適な資本構成だとはいえません。まず、その点を理解していただくところから始めました。
~~~~
――今回の共同策定は、自身が目指すアクティビズムにとって、どのような意味がありましたか。
われわれにとってもテストケースでした。投資銀行、PE（プライベートエクイティ）ファンド、経営コンサルティング出身者のノウハウを総動員し、経営陣と一緒に考えればここまでできる。新中計発表後の株価上昇も含めて、その可能性を示せたと思います。
投資先の経営陣はわれわれの提案を警戒しがちですが、フォスター電機の事例がその警戒感を和らげることを期待しています。単に投資リターンを上げるだけでなく、ファンドという形で社会にどんなソリューションを提供できるかを考えながら投資しています。
~~~~
フォスター電機は株価倍増の「1万円」も視野と新中計を共同策定したアクティビストが明言、資本政策“大転換”の舞台裏と今後の協業のあり方を激白

I'm cautiously optimistic about the market here.
Since 1980, we've had 22 instances where the S&P 500 experienced a correction of 10%.
Here's how the market historically performed after crossing that threshold:
- 3 months later: +4% on average, positive 73% of the time.
- 6 months later: +8% on average, positive 77% of the time.
- 12 months later: +10% on average, with a median return of 16%.
What's particularly interesting is that one month following a correction, the average return is essentially flat. Historically, recoveries haven't necessarily happened overnight, which is why I don't think there's any reason to rush into deploying all your cash at once.
We still have plenty of macro headwinds to work through, including inflation, potential rate hikes and political uncertainty but none of that changes my long term conviction in AI or the fundamentals of the companies I'm invested in. Historically, these corrections have more often been buying opportunities for long-term investors than reasons to panic.
You can be cautious in the short term while remaining incredibly bullish in the long term.

私はここの市場について慎重ながらも楽観的です。
1980 年以来、S&P 500 が 10% の調整を経験した例が 22 回ありました。
そのしきい値を超えた後の市場の過去のパフォーマンスは次のとおりです。
- 3 か月後: 平均 +4%、73% の確率でプラスになります。
- 6 か月後: 平均 +8%、77% の確率でプラス。
- 12 か月後: 平均 +10%、収益中央値は 16%。
特に興味深いのは、調整後 1 か月では平均リターンがほぼ横ばいであることです。歴史的に見て、回復は必ずしも一夜にして起こったわけではありません。だからこそ、急いですべての現金を一度に投入する理由はないと思います。
インフレ、利上げの可能性、政治的不確実性など、対処しなければならないマクロ的な逆風はまだたくさんありますが、そのいずれも、AI に対する私の長期的な信念や、私が投資している企業のファンダメンタルズを変えるものではありません。歴史的に、これらの調整は、長期投資家にとってパニックになる理由ではなく、買いの機会となることが多かったです。
長期的には信じられないほど強気でありながら、短期的には慎重になることができます。

The CEO of $ASML just told Washington something it is not going to want to hear.
The United States is considering rules that would stop ASML from servicing the DUV machines it has already sold in China. He said the factories would keep running anyway.
In his words, if you stop service, the fab keeps going. The only thing that happens is you lose control of your equipment.
His point is that if ASML pulls its engineers, another team will step in and do the work, including Japanese firms and local Chinese companies.
ASML's most advanced machines have already been kept out of China for almost 10 years and cutting off service on the tools that are already there would not stop those fabs.
It would only cost ASML its visibility and control.
Every new restriction gives China another reason to build its own equipment faster.
That is the long term risk I worry about for the western chip supply chain.
Milk Road AI (@MilkRoadAI)
New United States export rules took effect today, and TSMC is already tightening what Chinese chip designers can get made.
Reuters, citing two people familiar with the matter, said $TSM has told affected customers that orders using 16 nanometer technology and below will be halted unless they obtain a United States export license.
Those customers will generally be limited to older 28 nanometer and 40 nanometer processes, and not if the chips use high bandwidth memory or need advanced packaging.
The new rules removed a path that had let TSMC check a design's computing power to see whether it fell outside the controls. Advanced chips from affected Chinese customers are now presumed to be covered, Reuters said.
The Financial Times first reported that TSMC and Samsung have suspended some shipments to Chinese customers. Reuters said a United States list of approved designers includes $NVDA, $AMD, Apple, MediaTek, and Realtek, and no mainland Chinese firms.
We think this closes one of the last foundry routes for Chinese AI chips, though these accounts come from people familiar with the guidance, not from an official TSMC announcement.

TrendForce just put a number on a split I have been watching in the memory market.
Chinese cloud companies have cut their 2027 enterprise SSD orders by enough to cancel out the extra demand coming from North America, where cloud providers have actually raised their forecasts.
The cuts in China are being tied to GPU shortages, high inventories, and weaker AI monetization.
Consumer devices are also a drag, as brands cut storage specs to control costs.
Global NAND bit supply is still projected to grow 25% to 30% next year, and TrendForce says demand will not keep up and it expects the market to stay in oversupply all year.
NAND contract prices are forecast to be flat to down 5% in the first quarter of 2027, with every category declining from the second quarter onward.
This is the opposite of what I see in DRAM and HBM, where supply is still struggling to catch demand.
NAND is a different story, and $SNDK is more exposed to it than the HBM names.
Milk Road AI (@MilkRoadAI)
$MU is dealing with a split in the memory market that is becoming harder to ignore.
According to CFM Flash Market, memory makers cut prices this week on eMMC, LPDDR4X, and some industrial SSDs because demand is weak.
Buyers are mostly drawing down inventory, and actual transactions are limited and the cuts are concentrated in older, lower end products.
eMMC 256GB fell from $52.50 to $48.50, a drop of about 7.6%. Industrial SATA 512GB SSDs fell from $110 to $95, down almost 14%. LPDDR4X 32Gb and 64Gb were also marked down, while every LPDDR5X price on the list held flat.
NAND wafers and DDR5 chips were unchanged this week, and DDR5 modules are still sitting at record highs. PC makers in China and Taiwan remain cautious on new orders.
This lines up with what TrendForce just said. It raised its 2027 forecast for server DRAM, but it cut consumer DRAM and NAND because higher memory prices are hurting phones and PCs.
We think this is the split to watch for $MU, $SNDK, and $WDC. HBM, server DRAM, and DDR5 still look tight.
The weakness is showing up first in the legacy parts that go into phones, PCs, and older industrial systems.

Official CFO commentary said Nvidia's supply and capacity commitments jumped from $279 billion last quarter to $390 billion, primarily related to the multi year procurement of memory supply.

We are starting to see the early signs of a government bailout for the AI trade.
I think we're starting to see some pretty interesting developments over the last few days that suggest governments are becoming increasingly concerned about the selloff in financial markets. First, look at what just happened with Nvidia. Jensen Huang resigned, Nvidia's board initially made it clear that he would not be reinstated, and the entire AI trade continued getting absolutely hammered. Then President Trump personally got involved, reportedly pressured Nvidia's board to bring Jensen back, and suddenly Jensen is CEO again. That's a pretty extraordinary reversal, especially considering the board had ruled out his return just days earlier.
Then there's Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who initially called for a major leadership shake up at Nvidia and suggested the company needed an outside CEO. Fast forward a week, and his position softened considerably, even leaving the door open for Jensen to return. I find this particularly interesting because it suggests the administration's approach changed as the broader AI selloff continued putting pressure on financial markets.
And now look at what's happening in South Korea. The government is preparing to activate its stock market stabilization fund, a mechanism deployed during the 2008 global financial crisis. The fund allows financial institutions to pool capital and purchase equities during severe market declines to help stabilize prices. Now, I'm not suggesting we're heading into another 2008, nor am I saying the US government is preparing a direct stock market bailout. But I do think these developments show how seriously governments are beginning to take this selloff. AI has become such an important part of economic growth, capital investment, and financial markets that a prolonged collapse in the sector could have consequences far beyond technology stocks, especially considering the hundreds of billions of dollars being committed to AI infrastructure.
And just to be clear, I'm extremely bullish on AI over the long term. I'm by no means a bear on the sector, and I still believe we're in the early innings of one of the biggest technological transformations in history. I just wanted to point these developments out because I think they're worth paying attention to after everything we've experienced over the last couple of weeks. It's possible we're beginning to see governments take a more active role in restoring confidence. But we also have to remember that Jensen returning doesn't suddenly fix inflation, the possibility of additional interest rate hikes, or the broader macroeconomic uncertainty. I'm encouraged by what we're seeing, and I wouldn't be surprised if the AI trade stages a powerful recovery from here. But being bullish on AI long term doesn't mean we should ignore the risks in front of us today.

ここ数週間で私が学んだことの 1 つは、感情はいかに急速に変化するかということです。誰もが押し目ごとに買いたいと思っていた状態から、AI株に手を出したがる人はほとんどいない状態になり、今では突然楽観的な見方が戻ってきています。

On market crashes like today, I'm reminded of a piece of advice I got from a CIO mentor that traded during the dotcom and 08 crashes and lived to tell the tale.
He said: "Treat investing the same way you treat life."
That's all. It has stuck with me for many years because after filling in the blanks, you're forced to become "better" in both portfolio management and life management. It's uncanny how correlated they are.
Strip either one down and you're left with the same raw materials: time and uncertainty.
Every investment gives up something certain today for something uncertain tomorrow. So does nearly everything that matters in life. Love, learning, raising a child, starting a new job. Anything.
Both reward patience, but only after testing it.
You can't generate performance without risking losses, the same way you can't love without risking grief.
But fundamentally, the first rule of portfolio and life management is survival.
You can come back from most losses, but not from the one that takes you out of the game.
It's always darkest before the dawn.

Commodities are getting hit pretty hard alongside the broader equity market as the surging U.S. dollar sucks liquidity out of the global financial system. For those that follow me, I've been saying this from some time that there was risks if the dollar strengthens too quickly.
The issue is that dollar-denominated debt becomes more expensive to service, financial conditions tighten, and investors are forced to raise cash, reduce leverage and sell assets. It becomes less about fundamentals and more about liquidity.
One thing I've learned over the years is that market leverage doesn't necessarily tell you when a correction will happen, but it tells you a great deal about how painful that correction could become. For some perspective, U.S. margin debt has surged to approximately $1.45 trillion, equivalent to roughly 58% of U.S. currency in circulation and 6.2% of M2 money supply. That's an extraordinary amount of leverage in the system, and when markets start moving against investors, it can accelerate the selling pressure.
Unfortunately, even gold isn't immune. During a liquidity-driven selloff, investors often sell what they can, not necessarily what they want to. Gold can become a source of cash to cover margin calls and offset losses elsewhere.
The irony is that the very forces driving the dollar higher could eventually create the conditions for its reversal. The U.S. government and broader financial system have become increasingly reliant on negative real interest rates to help manage an enormous debt burden. A prolonged dollar-driven liquidity squeeze makes that increasingly difficult, raising the risk that something eventually breaks and forces central banks to step in with lower rates and additional liquidity.
That's when things can get interesting for gold. It may get sold during the initial panic, but if policymakers respond by driving real interest rates back into negative territory, the combination of easier money and renewed currency debasement concerns could send gold sharply higher.
In other words, the same liquidity squeeze hurting gold today could ultimately create the conditions for its next rally.
We're watching all of this closely and remaining deliberate about managing exposure through what continues to be a challenging market environment through to the end of the year.

米ドルの高騰が世界の金融システムから流動性を吸い取る中、株式市場全体と並んでコモディティもかなり大きな打撃を受けている。私を支持する人々のために、私は以前から、ドルが急激に上昇するとリスクがあると言い続けてきました。
問題は、ドル建て債務の返済コストが高くなり、金融状況が逼迫し、投資家が現金の調達、レバレッジの削減、資産の売却を余儀なくされていることだ。ファンダメンタルズよりも流動性が重要になります。
私が長年にわたって学んだことの 1 つは、市場レバレッジは調整がいつ起こるか必ずしも教えてくれるわけではありませんが、その調整がどれほど痛みを伴うものになる可能性があるかを大いに教えてくれるということです。ある見方をすると、米国の証拠金負債は約1兆4500億ドルまで急増しており、これは流通している米国通貨の約58％、M2マネーサプライの6.2％に相当する。これはシステムにおける異常なレバレッジであり、市場が投資家に不利な動きを始めると、売り圧力が加速する可能性があります。
残念ながら、金さえも影響を受けないわけではありません。流動性主導の下落では、投資家は売りたいものを売るわけではなく、売れるものを売ることがよくあります。金はマージンコールをカバーし、他の場所での損失を相殺するための現金源となる可能性があります。
皮肉なことに、ドルを上昇させるまさにその力が、最終的には反転の条件を生み出す可能性があるということだ。米国政府とより広範な金融システムは、マイナスの実質金利への依存度を高めています。

I covered this earlier in Jan regarding PCB bottlenecks with photonics + $AMZN Kuiper / $SPCX starlink supply chains.
But as an update, it like other industries outside of AI are really starting to feel the pain now too.
Global Electronics Association: "Is issuing this Industry Alert on escalating shortages across the printed circuit board (PCB) supply chain.
Companies in automotive, industrial, medical, defense, and telecommunications report longer lead times and difficulty securing supply as AI absorbs scarce capacity, effectively putting production at risk"
The association meaningful relief unlikely before mid-2028. The association urged buyers to plan ahead for supply constraints and manufacturers.
Hyperscalers like $AMZN already planned ahead of time taking stakes in Gold Circuit Electronics (2368) for supply procurement...
But can't say the same about other industries procurement (medical industry is probably not used to competing with hyperscalers over the same supply lol).
The resulting shortages of critical materials, including CCLs and fibreglass cloth, are squeezing supplies for consumer electronics.
TLDR: same bottleneck, same timeline for 2028. It's just interesting to see association warnings about it impacting medical to defense industries.
So there's incremental information that it's become an industry wide allocation issue.
I also think it's helpful to see escalating shortages + broadening... so it might show the selloff is starting to look very disconnected with fundamental demand.

しかし、最新情報として、AI 以外の他の業界と同様に、現在も実際に痛みを感じ始めています。
Global Electronics Association: 「プリント基板 (PCB) のサプライチェーン全体にわたる不足の深刻化に関して、この業界警報を発行しています。
自動車、産業、医療、防衛、電気通信の企業は、AIが不足している生産能力を吸収し、実質的に生産をリスクにさらしているため、リードタイムが長くなり、供給を確保することが困難であると報告しています。」
この協会による意味のある救済は、2028 年半ばまでに実現する可能性は低いです。同協会はバイヤーに対し、供給の制約やメーカーに備えて事前に計画を立てるよう呼び掛けた。
$AMZN のようなハイパースケーラーは、供給調達のために Gold Circuit Electronics (2368) の株式を取得することを事前に計画していました...
しかし、他の業界の調達については同じことは言えません（医療業界はおそらく同じ供給をめぐってハイパースケーラーと競争することに慣れていないでしょう笑）。
その結果、CCLやガラス繊維クロスなどの重要な材料が不足し、家庭用電化製品の供給が圧迫されています。
TLDR: 同じボトルネック、2028 年の同じタイムライン。医療業界から防衛業界に影響を与えるという協会の警告を見るのは興味深いことです。
したがって、これが業界全体の割り当て問題になっているという情報が増えています。
また、不足がエスカレートし、供給範囲が広がっていることも有益だと思います...したがって、下落が非常に切り離されているように見え始めていることを示す可能性があります

Markets appear to be wrongly interpreting Chinese eSSD cuts as deteriorating demand and NAND oversupply.
Phison CEO commentary today + more context behind $SNDK / Kioxia selloff regarding Trendforce revisions:
- "Pua attributed China's recent enterprise SSD demand slowdown to GPU shortages since November 2026"
- "Without GPUs, additional purchases offer little value, prompting some companies to sell server components on the spot market to recover cash"
(for context enterprise SSDs are growth driver for NAND)
- "Chinese cloud giants nevertheless plan substantial GPU prepayments, temporarily tying up capital and delaying procurement of other components."
- "the principal challenge in 2027 would be insufficient supply rather than weakening demand, with persistent AI shortages potentially prompting further procurement and inventory accumulation."
Markets seemed to have wrongly interpreted this as demand destruction + pricing collapse.
When Phison CEO attributed it to
-> GPU shortages
-> causing procurement timing mismatch
-> Chinese CSPs needed capital for GPU prepayments, so liquidation in inventory (causing spot price volatility)
-> timeline shift in order procurement
TLDR: delayed procurement from GPU shortages. there were actual order cuts, but this is deferred procurement not structural demand weakening.
Chinese CSPs needed capital for GPU prepayments so they liquidated other inventories in the meantime.
Phison says its inventories are insufficient for anticipated 2027 demand and it's sees this as an opportunity for NAND accumulation.
It's interesting the bottleneck in China migrated back to GPUs though.
items.title_ja:
市場は中国のeSSD削減を需要の悪化とNANDの供給過剰と誤って解釈しているようだ。
Phison CEO の今日のコメントと、Trendforce の改訂に関する $SNDK / Kioxia の売却の背後にある詳細な背景:
- 「Pua 氏は、2026 年 11 月以降の中国の最近のエンタープライズ SSD 需要の鈍化は GPU 不足によるものだと考えています」
- 「GPU がなければ、追加購入しても価値がほとんどないため、一部の企業は現金を回収するためにスポット市場でサーバー コンポーネントを販売するようになりました。」
(エンタープライズ SSD が NAND の成長ドライバーであるという背景から)
- 「それにもかかわらず、中国のクラウド大手は多額の GPU の前払いを計画しており、一時的に資本を拘束し、他のコンポーネントの調達を遅らせています。」
- 「2027年の主な課題は、需要の減退ではなく供給不足であり、持続的なAI不足がさらなる調達と在庫の蓄積を促す可能性がある。」
市場はこれを需要破壊＋価格崩壊と誤って解釈したようだ。
Phison CEO がその理由を挙げたとき
-> GPU不足
-> 調達タイミングのミスマッチが発生する
-> 中国の CSP は GPU 前払いのための資本を必要としたため、在庫を流動化しました (スポット価格の変動を引き起こす)
-> 注文調達のタイムラインの変化

SOME PERSONAL THOUGHTS AHEAD OF WEEKEND
I wanted to share a few thoughts heading into the weekend because at least for me this has been one of most mentally exhausting stretches I've experienced investing in growth stocks.
And honestly one of the things I've found most difficult has very little to do with market itself since it's how much mental real estate I apparently occupy in the minds of certain "gurus" on this platform whom I've never met, followed or even spoken to.
I started sharing my thoughts on X back in 2023 simply because I genuinely love investing and wanted somewhere to talk about market, share my research and connect with people who enjoyed it as much as I did and I never imagined that would turn into an account reaching 100 million impressions every month or that I'd eventually find myself appearing on national television every week.
I'm incredibly grateful because this platform accelerated my career at a relatively young age and opened doors that otherwise might have taken me many more years to reach but I'd be lying if I said spotlight wasn't intense since the larger my audience becomes and more visible I am the more I've realized that success also seems to attract resentment from people I've never interacted with or affected in any way possible.
Daniel has a phrase for this that I think captures it perfectly because "hating up" is absolutely real especially online where people seem more comfortable attacking someone who has become visible than examining why that person's success bothers them in the first place.
Like I've had people accuse me of taking an investment idea from them despite fact that I don't follow them and have never even seen their work while others take a disagreement over a particular thesis and turn it into a personal judgment about whether I know anything about investing.
What I find especially strange is that some of these individuals are in their 40s and 50s have been doing this for decades and still seem determined to tear down a 33 year old who is simply willing to publish his research, explain what he believes and put his own money behind those convictions (I've never asked anyone to agree with me or suggested that my way of investing is the only way to succeed).
And I think that last part is important because I do all of this under my real name and face, publicly disclose what I own through my subs service, share my position sizes and actual dollars I've invested and expose myself to scrutiny over every good decision and every mistake along the way.
There's absolutely nothing wrong with choosing to remain anonymous and I respect anyone who prefers to operate that way but theres just a different level of personal accountability when people know exactly who you are and watch you explain your thesis on camera and follow your positions in real time and wait for first opportunity to use a bad outcome against you... just remember being wrong privately costs you money but being wrong publicly can also cost you reputation, confidence and peace of mind which is something I don't think people fully appreciate until they've experienced it themselves.
None of this is to suggest that criticism should be off limits because disagreement is a huge part of investing but what I truly struggle to understand is why disagreement so often has to become personal... especially during periods like this when so many people are already dealing with painful drawdowns and questioning decisions they made with the best information available to them.
Markets eventually humble every single one of us regardless of how experienced we are or how much success we've had and anyone who stays in this long enough will eventually experience a thesis that breaks or a position they sized too aggressively or a drawdown that exposes a weakness in their process or a decision they wish they could take back so that's why I think showing people grace matters so much because you never know when you'll find yourself on the other side of that experience hoping others will extend you the same understanding.
And also just remember it cost absolutely nothing to root for people, respect the work they're putting in and recognize that someone can be wrong about an investment without deserving to be ridiculed for it and I genuinely wish more people on this platform understood that being publicly wrong doesn't erase courage it takes to stand behind your own convictions in the first place.
And to the people who've made rooting against me a hobby I genuinely hope you find the same energy for your own work that you've found for mine because if you're spending more time waiting for someone else to fail than building something of your own then maybe my portfolio isn't what needs your attention.
I'll be here next week, same name, same face, same conviction.

週末に向けての個人的な考え
少なくとも私にとって、これは成長株への投資で経験した中で最も精神的に疲れる作業の1つだったので、週末に向けていくつかの考えを共有したいと思いました。
そして正直に言うと、私が最も難しいと感じたことの1つは、市場自体とはほとんど関係がありません。それは、私が会ったことも、フォローしたことも、話したことさえない、このプラットフォーム上の特定の「達人」の心の中で私がどれだけの精神的領域を占めていると思われるかということだからです。
私が X についての考えを 2023 年に共有し始めたのは、単純に投資が心から好きで、市場について話したり、自分の研究を共有したり、同じように市場を楽しんでいる人々とつながる場所が欲しかったからです。それが毎月 1 億インプレッションに達するアカウントに成長したり、最終的には全国放送のテレビに毎週出演するようになるとは想像もしていませんでした。
このプラットフォームのおかげで、比較的若い年齢で私のキャリアが加速し、到達するまでにさらに何年もかかっていた可能性がある扉が開かれたので、非常に感謝しています。しかし、視聴者が増えて知名度が上がるほど、成功は、私がこれまで交流したことのない、あるいは何らかの影響を与えたことのない人たちからの怒りを引き寄せるようにも見えることに気づいたので、スポットライトが強くなかったと言ったら嘘になります。
ダニエルはこれについてのフレーズを持っていますが、これはそれを完璧に捉えていると思います。なぜなら、「憎しみ」は絶対に現実のもので、特にオンラインでは、人々は誰かを調べるよりも、目立つようになった人を攻撃する方が安心しているようです。

items.title:
What do you think of Broadcom $AVGO stock going forward?
Broadcom stock is currently down 9.4% so far in 2026 ... AVGO is currently the 11th largest company in the world worth $1.496 Trillion
Do you think AVGO is a good buy here or does it have more work to the downside
VanquishTrader (@VanquishTrader)
$AVGO COULD BE SETTING UP FOR A MONSTER 2027
One of the biggest comeback stories in 2027 could be Broadcom as the semiconductor market may focus too much on the recent declines, gross margin contraction, and $GOOGL custom silicon hurdles and, therefore, completely ignore one of the most dramatic inflections in semiconductor earnings in the space.
Broadcom has been spending years designing custom AI accelerators, as well as networking and optical systems to go with them. All of that R&D is now going to transition into a massive commercialization event, which will be one of the largest in the history of the semiconductor space.
This is a company of Broadcom’s scale, with Q3 revenues up 86% to $29.6B, with AI semiconductor revenues up 221% to $16.7B in Q3, with management outlining AI revenues of $58B in fiscal 2026, which could double to $115B in fiscal 2027, only to double again in fiscal 2028 to $230B.
And to the extent that there is risk in this scenario, Hock Tan has ensured the required manufacturing capacity to support these projected revenues, only to have the resulting demand exceed the allocated capacity of the company.
Importantly, Broadcom’s largest customer, Google, is currently trying to diversify Broadcom-designed TPU shipments to MediaTek and $MRVL, but that does not necessarily mean that Google is trying to eliminate Broadcom from the TPU custom silicon space, only to diversify across several different semiconductor program designs.
Furthermore, the economics of AI computing are increasingly moving in the direction of custom silicon, with much of this to be used in conjunction with general purpose processing from $NVDA.
The growing percentage of AI workloads devoted to inference (i.e. the actual production of useful intelligence) creates enormous economic incentive for the hyperscalers and frontier AI companies to optimize their respective computing infrastructure to produce intelligence at the lowest possible cost.
In terms of semiconductor content, this translates into custom designed XPUs, for specific workloads, in addition to much larger amounts of networking and optical semiconductor content.
The company’s Tomahawk switching platforms, optical DSPs, high performance lasers and emerging co-packaged optics all will see enormous increases in semiconductor content per unit of computing as bandwidth becomes an increasingly critical component to high performance computing.
Today, Broadcom already generates enormous amounts of free cash flow ($13.7B in quarterly terms) and operating income (adjusted for non cash items, $20.1B in the most recent quarter). Management projects operating margins of 66% in Q4′17, after a number of quarters of declining gross margins due to increasing mix of complex AI systems and high cost memory.
I’ve also considered that growth from the upcoming AI selloff. While a short-term anxiety for Broadcom, I believe the market is currently underestimating the scale of growth coming from future customer Anthropics.
The IPO of and subsequent funding rounds from investors of more than $100 billion in capital will greatly enhance Anthropics rapid enterprise adoption in need of dedicated computing to address their intelligence scale needs instead of paying a premium for short-term access to Broadcom’s planned and yet to be converted to shipped AI deployments.
Funding commitments will translate to recognized revenue however, and while Broadcom’s providing of residual value support on portions of the financing is beneficial, Google’s recently reported reduction in shipment of certain Broadcom designed TPUs with corresponding increase in design of TPUs for shipment by alternative semiconductor designers such as MediaTek and Marvell will become an additional competitive concern for investors to consider and monitor.
The depth of Broadcom’s current penetration into complex custom silicon for the TPU based computing market is substantial and should not be confused with Broadcom’s losing all strategic value to such a large future customer indenning strategic, alternating amongst designers of multiple semiconductor solutions for optimal set of characteristics for deployment in computing needs of such a large future customer. In addition to Google, other frontier companies such as OpenAI and Meta are designing and deploying their own customized silicon for AI computing needs.
Nvidia’s recent growth and increasing dominance in the field of AI computing will create additional economic reasons forhyperscalers such as Google to design and deploy customsilicon based accelerators in addition to their NVIDIA provided general-purpose accelerators.
So Broadcom could be one of the biggest comeback trades of the year as investors focus on the wrong part of the company’s semiconductor business. With the stock down to $313 or so, Broadcom could double or so in the space of a few years as earnings grow by 10% or so per year for several years in a row.
That said, a lot of things could go wrong. The worst that could happen is that Google’s diversification of TPU suppliers to companies like MediaTek and Marvell could reduce Broadcom’s portion of TPU spending dramatically.
And it’s possible that the huge growth in Broadcom’s AI semiconductor business could quickly fizzle out as customers struggle to deploy these increasingly complex computers.
Moreover, Broadcom’s increasingly large customer-financing commitment of residual value could become a big negative for the stock as Broadcom’s customers increasingly default on their obligations, which in turn could negatively impact Broadcom’s earnings. But none of these potential negatives would necessarily impact the stock’s potential to double or so in a few years, as I outlined above.
Instead, the big variable is whether Broadcom can in fact turn its pipeline of promising products into real operating leverage and higher earnings per share over time. And so, in terms of earnings growth and free cash flow, I think Broadcom could be a big comeback trade in 2027.
The December 9th earnings report will be a huge test for the semiconductor and AI computing stock and option positions that I have taken, in terms of growth in semiconductor revenues for AI computing, as well as growth in the company’s gross margin.
Finally, if the company’s AI semiconductor business does in fact deliver on the extremely promising near-term and longer-term earnings growth and free cash flow that I outlined above, then Broadcom could become one of the biggest and most important earners in the entire AI economy, over the space of the next two years or so.

Broadcom の株価は、2026 年現在までに 9.4% 下落しています...AVGO は現在、世界で 11 番目に大きな企業であり、その価値は 1.496 兆ドルです

Broadcom は、カスタム AI アクセラレータと、それに付随するネットワークおよび光学システムの設計に何年も費やしてきました。これらすべての研究開発は現在、半導体分野の歴史の中で最大規模となる大規模な商品化イベントに移行しようとしています。

そして、このシナリオにリスクがある限り、ホック・タンはこれらの予測収益をサポートするために必要な製造能力を確保しましたが、結果として生じる需要は会社に割り当てられた能力を超えるだけでした。
